title: Vanadium was discovered twice (and the first time was in Mexico)

scenes.text: The metal that hardens the steel in your tools was discovered twice. And the first time was in Mexico.
The year is 1801. Andrés Manuel del Río, professor of mineralogy in Mexico City, analyzes a lead mineral… and finds a new element.
He sends a sample to Paris. The French chemists reply: it's not new, it's a chromium mineral. They were wrong, but the discovery was set aside.
Thirty years later, the Swede Sefström finds it again, in cast iron. He proves it is new and names it: vanadium, after Vanadis, a Norse goddess.
That is why Del Río's name is nowhere on the periodic table. But the Royal Society of Chemistry puts it in writing: discovered in 1801 by Andrés Manuel del Río.
Share it with someone who thinks science always gets it right the first time.
